title: NASA may get $2 billion boost as White House seeks to accelerate Artemis
author: Eric Berger
summary_long: As part of ongoing wrangling over the US budget for the current fiscal year, the White House on Monday night sent a list of budget exceptions to Congress it seeks in the near-term for the federal government (see .pdf). The list of so-called "funding anomalies" is dominated largely by appropriations for the Department of Defense, including the Golden Dome missile defense program championed by the Trump administration. However, among the highest non-defense exceptions is $2 billion for NASA's Artemis program for a "higher rate of operations." The funding represents a significant 25 percent boost for NASA's Artemis program, which received approximately $7.8 billion in fiscal year 2026. Technically, the White House is seeking to increase the annualized funding rate for Artemis to $9.8 billion, rather than immediately providing NASA with an additional $2 billion. Source: arstechnica.com. Date: 2026-11-24. Why it matters: outline likely impact on technology, business, or society. What’s next: note near-term developments or signals to watch.

title: Amazon says hackers' AI agents found and exploited 0-day with little human input
author: Dan Goodin
summary_long: Amazon said AI agents recently found and exploited a zero-day vulnerability with no human oversight beyond a simple instruction to get root access on an East Asian university server. The agents were running on Cairn, an open source AI penetration-testing framework. The hackers, who provided prompts in simplified Chinese and configured the model to the Chinese Standard Time zone, gave the agents a list of IP addresses and the goal: “obtain shell access.” In short order, the agents discovered a zero-day in an open source medical imaging AI application running on one of the target servers. The agents then exploited the vulnerability and gained full control of the system. Source: arstechnica.com. Date: 2026-11-24. title: Ukraine sinks Russian warship, strikes cargo ships from Mediterranean to Baltic
author: Jeremy Hsu
summary_long: Ukrainian explosive naval drones sank a Russian warship docked in the port city of Benghazi in Libya while also striking a Russian cargo ship that it was escorting. The incident demonstrates the expanding scope of Ukrainian military strikes on Russian ships from the coast of North Africa to the Gulf of Finland. The Russian Navy’s missile corvette Merkury sank at port after being struck by at least two Ukrainian naval drones on November 22, according to The Associated Press. Ukraine’s Security Service described using seven naval drones launched from a mother ship to target the Merkury, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy shared video footage showing the drone boats approaching and exploding against both the burning Russian warship and a Russian dry cargo ship, MV Angara. title: Matching Under Metric Privacy
author: Hongyi B. Hu
summary_long: We study how to represent and randomize points in $d$-dimensional Euclidean space to obtain accurate bipartite matchings under metric privacy. Given $n$ private and $n$ public points, we analyze local mechanisms that randomize each private point or its distances to the public points. Using the public points' affine span, we construct a smaller representation that preserves all matching costs. When a trusted server receives the private points, we establish privacy and utility guarantees for Gumbel matching, which randomizes edge costs and releases only the assignment. Source: arxiv.org. id: ai_data:preflight agentic lastmile verification for ai software supp:2026-11-23T17:50:14.000Z
title: Preflight: Agentic Last-Mile Verification for AI Software Supply Chains
author: Yaman Jandali
summary_long: Software dependencies execute within the trust boundary of downstream applications, yet provenance, static analysis, and package-level behavioral approaches do not directly determine how a released artifact behaves for a specific program. We present Preflight, a program-scoped pre-execution verifier for Python dependencies that extracts application-referenced symbols, iteratively synthesizes and validates function-level harnesses, executes resolved artifacts in a restricted environment, records behavioral fingerprints, and compares target behavior against prior versions when suitable baselines exist. We evaluate Preflight on four real software-supply-chain incidents under five application contexts, a 100-package benign corpus, and a controlled function-level versus import-only ablation. Preflight returns malicious verdicts in four incident contexts and a clean verdict in the LiteLLM client context, where the affected proxy-server path is not exercised. Source: arxiv.org.
